text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- European Commission imposes a ban on export of live pigs from Netherlands. (p1)
- Philips software unit Origin plunges into the red with losses of 108 million. (p1)
- Unilever Plc chief Niall Fitzgerald says company will reconsider investment in Britain if it doesn't join EMU.(p1)
- Amsterdam AEX share index closes above 700 mark for first time. (p1)
- Electrical appliances maker Holec to apply for bourse listing in autumn. (p3)
- Brewer Heineken is preparing to close brewery in Zaire. (p3)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Philips president Cor Boonstra's tough restructuring policy has divided the company's management board. (p1)
- Stagnant CD sales forces Philips classical music label to sever recording ties with top conductor Bernard Haitink after relationship of 40 years. (p1)
- Paper and packaging concern KNP BT sees 1996 net profit halved to Dfl 231 million. (p33)
- Chemicals concern DSM to cooperate in engineering plastics with Japan Synthetic Rubber (JSR). (p33)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Traffic minister Annemarie Jorritsma is preparing drastic measures to curb Amsterdam Schiphol Airport's growth. (p1)
- Interactive CD flop will lead to damages claims against Philips from publishers. (p33)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Stork, Begemann group and Malaysian financier have new plan to relaunch bankrupt aircraft maker Fokker. (p1)
- Software company Baan takes over Germany's Straessle Informationssysteme. (p11)
